summary: Jinchuan Wan specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Wan held posts as professor at National Central University and Fo Guang University, both attested in 2010.
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995). Yin served as Director at the University of Hong Kong, attested between 2006 and 2010.

Jing-shen Tao is a sinologist and historian. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1959) and earned a Ph.D. from Indiana University Bloomington (~1963–1967). He served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000).
Jingru Wang (1903–1990) worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1928–1932) and later held a post at Minzu University of China.
Jingyi Yang works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational fields. Yang studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin, attested in 2026.

Jinhua Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Chen completed graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research under Noritoshi Aramaki at Kyoto University. Chen held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 2001) and University of British Columbia (attested 2008–2018).

Jinhua Jia is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder (1994–1999) under Paul W. Kroll. Jia held posts at Harvard University and the University of Macau (Adjunct Professor, 2020).
Jinling He is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, where he studied under supervisor Hiroki Okumura.
Jinping Liao specializes in Buddhist studies. Liao completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

Jinshi Fan works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Su Bai (~1958–1963), served as Director of Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014), and held a post at Lanzhou University.

Jinzhang Peng (1937–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He served at Wuhan University until 1986 and was a researcher and archaeological institute dean at Dunhuang Academy from ~1986 to 2017.
Jiro Abe (1883–1959) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1907). He later held academic posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita (1920–2009) worked in Tibetology and other fields. After studying at Kyoto University (~1940–1943), he held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1967–1977), University of Tsukuba (~1977–1985), and Chubu University (~1985).

Jiro Murata (1895–1985) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920) and held a post at National Institute of Technology, Akashi College (~1962–1968).

Jiro Sugiyama (1928–2011) specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952), he held posts at Tokyo National Museum (attested 1984–1986) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996).
Jiryo Masuda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Unrai Wogihara and served as a professor at the University of Calcutta.
Jishu Oda (1908–1989) worked in Buddhist studies. He was attested as Rector at Choboji Monastery in 1914 and as an emeritus professor at Shuchiin University in 1977.

Jitendra Nath Banerjea (1895–1966) worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

Jitendra Nath Mohanty (1928–2023) was a philosopher and Indologist. He studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Göttingen (Ph.D. ~1952–1954). He held teaching posts at Calcutta, Oklahoma, and Temple University (Professor ~1986–2008).
Jitsushyu Oshika (born 1919) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Oshika studied at Tohoku University and held a post as professor at Toyo University, attested in 1980–1981.
